messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I'm seeing gaps when joining app request logs to traces in us-central1 after last night's autoscale. Correlation headers (X-Corr-ID) are present on the ingress but not on many backend logs.
Maya: saw the pager for loki-ingest-rate earlier, could be ingestion sharding causing drops. SREBot: ALERT loki_ingest_rate_drop firing for tenant=redwood-main :rate drops > 40% (03:12 UTC)
Devon: running a quick Loki query to check missing header patterns. Query:
```
{job="app-frontend", cluster="us-central1"} |~ "X-Corr-ID" | line_format "{app} {pod} {X-Corr-ID}"
```
Devon: results show a subset of pods (app-backend-v2-*) with empty header lines between 03:00-03:10. Other pods (v1) look fine.
Kai: we rotated some preemptible GPU nodes in that window for scale-down -> scale-up. kube-proxy restarted briefly on a few nodes per the node-ops runbook.
Alex: do we have any evidence of proxy restart dropping sidecar forwarders or promtail connections? That would explain correlation missing at ingestion.
Maya: promtail logs show frequent reconnects around 03:05. Command I used:
```
kubectl -n observability logs promtail-5f8 -c promtail | grep "reconnect" -n
```
Maya: also saw a parity issue: our promtail relabel config drops headers for files > 1MB due to the current pipeline, which can happen with stacked logs during restart.
Devon: confirmed — for app-backend-v2 the log rotation/size heuristics triggered and promtail dropped headers. Repro steps attached: reproduce by nuking kube-proxy on node and generating high-volume logs.
Alex: what about traces? Did the tracer library inject the X-Corr-ID or rely solely on upstream header?
Kai: library uses header if present, otherwise falls back to generated trace-id but we don't attach that back into stdout logs. So when header lost mid-path, backend logs lose linking key.
Maya: short-term mitigation: adjust promtail pipeline to preserve the X-Corr-ID label regardless of chunk size. I can push a hotfix to observability helm chart.
Devon: also patching backend runtime to echo trace id into logs when tracing context exists — low-risk change.
SREBot: DEPLOYMENT promtail-hotfix triggered by Maya at 04:12 UTC — rolling update across observability namespace.
Alex: after the hotfix, re-run the original Loki join test. Devon can you run the join query across 03:00-04:30 and report if X-Corr-ID density recovers?
Devon: ran it. Post-hotfix we see correlation presence jump from ~58% -> ~98% for the same pod set. Loki ingest rate alert cleared around 04:20.
Kai: for follow-up: (1) tune promtail chunking thresholds to avoid future header toss, (2) add a small exporter metric for "promtail_header_dropped" so we can alert before customer-visible gaps, (3) update autoscaler runbook to drain a node differently for pods with sidecar state.
Maya: agreed. I'll open infra ticket and update dashboards. Suggest changing alert flapping window to 10m to reduce noise when autoscaler legitimately moves capacity.
Alex: thanks all. Filing a post-incident note and scheduling a short retro. TL;DR — node rotation + promtail chunking edge case caused correlation header loss; hotfix restored links. :thumbsup:
